Figure_CMFA_before_after_heatmaps: Actual feature responses before and after CMFA in three Mobile validation images. The same DENT-STRIDE-Mobile checkpoint (seed 2; prototype temperature 0.50) supplies every panel. Before denotes concatenation of the two spatially aligned inputs. All before and after responses are channel RMS with one shared color scale across the three images; the upper display limit is the pooled 99.5th percentile within the displayed crops. The difference map is RMS(after) minus RMS(before), with red indicating increased magnitude and blue decreased magnitude; it is not the RMS of the vector difference. The same crop and image registration are used within each row. Row (a) shows an oral overview; rows (b,c) show local incisor regions centered on reference FDI 41 and 81, respectively. These are actual feature-response maps, not attention probabilities or Grad-CAM; stronger responses do not by themselves establish improved detection.

Figure_Mobile_factor_fusion_before_after: Same-checkpoint effect of factor-score fusion in Mobile images. The trained DENT-STRIDE-Mobile seed-2 checkpoint (prototype temperature 0.50) is unchanged; inference fusion weights are zero in the off condition and 0.10/0.05/0.03 for quadrant/position/dentition in the on condition. (a) The highest-scoring FDI of the same query changes from 16 to the reference 55. (b) It changes from 65 to the reference 64. (c) An adverse example changes the correct 81 to 41. Identical local crops are used across columns; ground truth is teal and predictions orange. Only the target ground-truth box and the highest-scoring class of the tracked query are annotated; other class candidates can coexist in native top-300 outputs. Both tracked predictions have score >=0.30 and localization IoU >=0.50. Model weights, query boxes, and native postprocessing are unchanged. These examples illustrate score reordering, not the effect of training without factor-head supervision or the population frequency of corrections.
